name: Railways

levels.note: No ITI. Minimum 10th + age 18–33 (relaxations apply). Physical standards in notification.
12th pass. Typing test where stated. Age 18–33.

posts.name: Technician (Fitter, Welder, Electrician, Diesel, AC, Machinist, Crane)
Junior Engineer (Civil, Electrical, Mechanical, Signal, Tele)

levels.note: NCVT/SCVT ITI certificate or AICTE diploma. Trade test for Technician; document verification for JE.
Any recognised degree. Station Master has Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT).

stages.name: CBT 1
stages.tests: 75 questions, 60 min. Mathematics, General Intelligence, General Science, General Awareness.
stages.note: Qualifying nature; score used for shortlisting to CBT 2. Negative marking 1/3.

stages.name: CBT 2
stages.tests: 75 questions, 60 min. Same subjects, higher difficulty. Trade-relevant questions for Technician.
stages.note: Merit prepared from CBT 2 normalized score.

stages.name: Typing / Skill Test
stages.tests: Typing: 30 wpm English / 25 wpm Hindi (10 min). Trade test for Technician as per trade syllabus.
stages.note: Qualifying only; does not add to merit.

stages.name: CBAT (Station Master)
stages.tests: 5 test batteries: memory, attention, spatial, reasoning, psychomotor. 90 min total.
stages.note: Qualifying. Only for Station Master candidates who clear CBT 2.

stages.name: Document Verification + Medical
stages.tests: All original certificates, caste, domicile, NOC. Medical standard A-2 / B-1 / C-1 per post.
stages.note: Final appointment only after medical fitness.

ladder: Senior Section Engineer / Technician Gr. I (Level 5–6)
Assistant Divisional Engineer / Depot Material Superintendent (Level 7)
reality: RRB notifications come in cycles (CEN). A single CEN advertises 10,000–100,000+ posts across zones.
CBT 1 is qualifying — clearing it does not guarantee a job. 5–10× the vacancies are called for CBT 2.
Trade test for Technician is hands-on; many who clear CBT 2 fail the practical.
Station Master CBAT is unique — no books prepare you. Practice with railway psychometric apps.
Medical standard is strict. Colour blindness knocks out Signal/Tele; BMI limits for heavy trades.
Zones publish their own panels after the centralised RRB merit. No inter-zone transfer in first posting.

faq.q: How many Railway zones and RRBs are there?
faq.a: 18 Railway zones, each with a Railway Recruitment Board (RRB). RRBs conduct centralised exams (CEN) for Group C/D posts; zones do final panel and appointment.

faq.q: Can a 10th pass apply for Technician posts?
faq.a: No. Technician requires ITI/NCVT in the specific trade. 10th pass applies for Group D (Level 1) posts like Track Maintainer, Pointsman, Helper.

faq.q: What is the difference between RRB NTPC and RRB Group D?
faq.a: NTPC = Non-Technical Popular Categories (graduate/12th posts: Clerk, Station Master, Goods Guard, Typist). Group D = Level 1 posts (Track Maintainer, Helper, Pointsman). Separate CENs, separate exams.

faq.q: Is there negative marking in RRB exams?
faq.a: Yes, 1/3 mark deducted per wrong answer in both CBT 1 and CBT 2. No negative marking in typing test, trade test, or CBAT.

faq.q: Where do I find the official RRB notification?
faq.a: Each RRB website (e.g., rrbmumbai.gov.in, rrbchennai.gov.in) and the central portal rrb.indianrailways.gov.in. SarkariJobs+ links the official PDF on every listing page.
You apply to one RRB (zone) per notification. Preference is for that zone. Inter-zone transfers are not allowed in the first appointment.
